elements.element: The licence extends to Customer's affiliates.
elements.evidence: The grant expressly includes Customer's Affiliates.

elements.element: The licence extends to contractors acting on Customer's behalf.
elements.evidence: The grant expressly includes contractors acting on Customer's behalf.
The clause contains no perpetual duration language. The possibility that the licence is or may become paid-up is not demonstrably absent.
The clause does not make paid-up licences irrevocable and instead permits revocation of the licence for an uncured material breach.

elements.element: Subscription licences are terminable only for an uncured material breach.
elements.evidence: The grant is revocable only for Customer's material breach that remains uncured following written notice and a reasonable opportunity to cure. This restriction applies generally and therefore covers any subscription licence.

elements.element: The licence is transferable to successors.
elements.evidence: The clause contains no transfer right for successors.

elements.element: Customer's affiliates are covered upon written notice.
elements.evidence: Affiliates are covered unconditionally, which is broader than coverage becoming effective upon written notice.

elements.element: The licence is transferable to a successor in an M&A transaction.
elements.evidence: The clause contains no transfer right for a successor in an M&A transaction.

result.reason: The redline successfully extends the grant to Affiliates and contractors and limits revocation to uncured material breach. It does not address perpetual and irrevocable treatment for paid-up licences or transferability to successors, including M&A successors, so neither the preferred nor fallback position is complete. The changes preserve the original use limitations and software restrictions, but the drafting is incomplete and leaves Affiliates and contractors as direct licensees without expressly subjecting them to the restrictions imposed only on Customer.
